# measoshapes

The goal of measoshapes is to provide the regions of the Marine Ecosystem Assessment for the
Southern Ocean (MEASO): five sectors (Atlantic, Central Indian, East Indian, West Pacific, East
Pacific), each with three zones (Antarctic, Subantarctic, Northern), as described in the MEASO
Summary for Policymakers (see [References](#references)).

The current version of the regions is **06**. Version 05 is kept as it was released.

Website: <https://australianantarcticdivision.github.io/measoshapes/>

## Installation

To install measoshapes from Github use

```R
## install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("AustralianAntarcticDivision/measoshapes")
```

## Map

To map the regions with base plotting (with the [sf package](https://r-spatial.github.io/sf)). There
is one row per region, with its `name`, `label`, `sector`, `zone`, and `fill` colour. The `_coastline`
form has the Antarctic continent cut out.

```{r plot, fig.alt = "Polar map of the 20 MEASO regions (version 06) in their fill colours, with the Antarctic continent cut out."}
library(measoshapes)
library(sf)

measo <- measo_regions06_coastline
plot(st_geometry(measo), col = measo$fill, border = "grey40")
```

The temperate (T) regions in the north of each sector are outside MEASO and have no fill.

```{r names}
sf::st_drop_geometry(measo)
```

## Map with ggplot2

To use the literal fill colours we need `scale_fill_identity()`, this is ggplot's "straight-through"
mechanism.

```{r ggplot2, fig.alt = "The same map of the MEASO regions made with ggplot2."}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(measo, aes(fill = fill)) + geom_sf(colour = "grey40") + scale_fill_identity()
```

## Map with SOmap

The [SOmap package](https://github.com/AustralianAntarcticDivision/SOmap) provides some simpler ways
of creating and adding to polar maps. Once a map is set up it knows what projection it is in, so we can
forget about having to transform the data.

```{r SOmap, eval = FALSE}
## TODO: SOplot() no longer adds to the SOmap() plot with current SOmap, not evaluated for now
library(SOmap)
SOmap(trim = -32) ## set up a polar map
## set overlay to half-transparent
SOplot(st_geometry(measo), border = NA, col = scales::alpha(measo$fill, 0.75))
```

## Data sets

There is no code in the measoshapes package, but the package records the creation of each data set
using standard R mechanisms (see 'data-raw/').

Version 06, one row for each of the 20 regions:

* `measo_regions06` polar Lambert Azimuthal Equal Area (use this for areas)
* `measo_regions06_ll` longitude/latitude
* `measo_regions06_coastline`, `measo_regions06_ll_coastline` with the Antarctic continent cut out
* `measo_names06` the `name`, `label`, `sector`, `zone`, and `fill` of each region

The longitude/latitude polygons are defined in *planar* longitude/latitude: boundaries follow parallels
and meridians, rather than great circles. The polar forms are densified (to 0.2 degree) so they follow
the same boundaries. In longitude/latitude the West Pacific regions are in two parts, either side of the
anti-meridian.

To export to shapefile:

```{r exportshp1, eval = FALSE}
st_write(measo_regions06_ll_coastline, "myfile.shp")
```

## Files

The version 06 regions are also provided as files in 'inst/extdata', created by 'data-raw/export.R',
with one row for each region (20 rows) and the same columns. They are also published on the
[website](https://australianantarcticdivision.github.io/measoshapes/).

* `measo_regions06.parquet`, `.fgb` polar Lambert Azimuthal Equal Area (equivalent to EPSG:6932), use this for areas
* `measo_regions06_ll.parquet`, `.fgb`, `.geojson` longitude/latitude (OGC:CRS84)
* `measo_regions06_epsg_3031.parquet`, `.fgb` Antarctic Polar Stereographic (EPSG:3031), e.g. for Quantarctica
* `measo_regions06.qml` a QGIS style with the fill colours and labels

```{r parquet, eval = FALSE}
f <- system.file("extdata/measo_regions06.parquet", package = "measoshapes")
x <- sf::read_sf(f)
```

The geopackages (`measo_regions.gpkg`, `measo_regions_ll.gpkg`, `measo_regions_epsg_3031.gpkg`) are
version 05 files, kept as they were.

## Version 05

Version 05 is kept as it was released:

* `measo_regions05`, `measo_regions05_ll`, `measo_regions05_coastline`, `measo_regions05_ll_coastline`
  the 24 polygons (geometry only)
* `measo_names` the `name`, `sector`, `zone`, and `fill` of each polygon, in the same order

WestPacific is split at the anti-meridian, so its names appear twice and `measo_names` is not a key. To
join the names to the geometry, group the features by name (removing the seam at the anti-meridian)
and join to the distinct names. The two WPA rows of `measo_names` have different fills (row 1 is a
known error), so this takes the first.

```{r join05}
library(dplyr)
measo05 <- measo_regions05 %>% group_by(name) %>% summarize() %>%
  inner_join(distinct(measo_names, name, .keep_all = TRUE), "name")
```

The northern regions are assigned codes that include "T" for **temperate**, but they aren't part of
MEASO. They share a sector but have no assigned zone.

```{r dummy, fig.alt = "Longitude/latitude map of the 24 version 05 polygons, coloured by sector and labelled with their names, with world coastlines."}
## label positions from the (equal area) polar form
cds <- st_coordinates(st_transform(st_centroid(measo_regions05), 4326))
par(mar = rep(0.2, 4))
plot(st_geometry(measo_regions05_ll), reset = FALSE,
     col = colourvalues::colour_values(measo_names$sector, alpha = 0.5))
text(cds, lab = measo_names$name, cex = 0.7)
maps::map(add = TRUE)
```

## References

The MEASO assessment areas (sectors and zones) are described in the MEASO Summary for Policymakers
(Figure 5, "MEASO assessment areas", adapted from McCormack et al. 2021). See also
`citation("measoshapes")`.

* Constable, A.J., J. Melbourne-Thomas, M.M.C. Muelbert, S. McCormack, M. Brasier, J.A. Caccavo,
  R.D. Cavanagh, S.M. Grant, H.J. Griffiths, J. Gutt, S.F. Henley, J. Höfer, A.B. Hollowed,
  N.M. Johnston, S.A. Morley, E.J. Murphy, M.H. Pinkerton, I.R. Schloss, K.M. Swadling,
  A.P. Van de Putte (2023) Marine Ecosystem Assessment for the Southern Ocean: Summary for
  Policymakers. Integrated Climate and Ecosystem Dynamics in the Southern Ocean, Scientific Committee
  on Antarctic Research, Scientific Committee on Oceanic Research, Integrated Marine Biosphere Research.
  <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8359585>
* McCormack, S.A., J. Melbourne-Thomas, R. Trebilco, J.L. Blanchard, B. Raymond, A. Constable (2021)
  Decades of dietary data demonstrate regional food web structures in the Southern Ocean. Ecology and
  Evolution 11(1): 227–241. <https://doi.org/10.1002/ece3.7017>

Earlier MEASO documents, from the time of versions 03 to 05 of the regions:

* Brasier, M.J., A. Constable, J. Melbourne-Thomas, R. Trebilco, H. Griffiths, A. Van de Putte,
  M. Sumner (2019) Observations and models to support the first Marine Ecosystem Assessment for the
  Southern Ocean (MEASO). Journal of Marine Systems 197: 103182.
  <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmarsys.2019.05.008>
* Constable, A., J. Melbourne-Thomas, R. Trebilco, M. Brasier (2018) Marine Ecosystem Assessment for
  the Southern Ocean (MEASO). SC-CCAMLR 2018 Background Paper, SC-CAMLR-XXXVII/BG/22.
  <https://figshare.utas.edu.au/articles/report/SC-CCAMLR_2018_Background_Paper_Marine_Ecosystem_Assessment_for_the_Southern_Ocean_MEASO_/23193956>
* Constable, A., J. Melbourne-Thomas, R. Trebilco, M. Sumner, M. Brasier (2018) The role of models in
  facilitating the first Marine Ecosystem Assessment for the Southern Ocean (MEASO). Australian Coastal
  and Oceans Modelling and Observations meeting, Canberra, October 2018.
  <https://figshare.utas.edu.au/articles/conference_contribution/The_role_of_models_in_facilitating_the_first_Marine_Ecosystem_Assessment_for_the_Southern_Ocean_MEASO_/23154533>
